Every outage is fully investigated by our engineers, though power may be lost several times before we can safely find and fix the issue. Our customer services team will keep as many customers updated as possible during these investigations.

To talk to us, or let us know that your power isn't restored, call us on 08003163105.

Sent by Simon at 16:38 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Sent by Kevin at 15:42 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Sent by Decasta at 19:51 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations. If you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Kevin at 16:05 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Specialist engineers are also working to divert power remotely, and this can cause your lights to go on and off. We know that a power cut can be very disruptive, even more so if you are vulnerable. If you're worried about an elderly or ill person in your property who is affected by the power cut today, we are able to provide some support. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress but for any concerns or questions, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. For more information on how we support vulnerable customers just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Decasta at 19:45 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Decasta at 19:49 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations. If you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Talie at 01:12 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Kings Lynn PE33 area should be back on. The issue was caused by a tree falling on our overhead cabling, which our engineers have now diverted power around. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual.

Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
We're sorry we've not been able to restore your power yet. We appreciate it can be unsettling to have a power cut during the night, but our engineers work 24 hours on issues like this so we're still aiming to have power restored as soon as possible.

If you light candles, please be mindful of them and take extra care when using the stairs. If you have any concerns, please call us on 105 and our team will help. We'll keep you updated. Sent by Theo at 00:04
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Jack at 22:30 - Hello again. Thanks for bearing with us during the power cut, I know the lights being off is a worry.

Our staff have advised that there is still a lot of repairs needed and the heavy rain and wind has caused delays. Due to the delay this has caused, they've advised a new time of 00:30-01:30 to have your power back on.

I know another delay is frustrating; our engineers always try to give us the best estimate that they can but due to the safety elements of working with live electricity, sometimes they have to adjust their repairs at short notice.

I'm sorry if this has caused you to change any plans you've made, but we'll be here to update you until the lights are safely back on.

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Our engineers have now arrived on site in the Fulham Road area.

As any issues that currently exist on our network have affected our equipment at the substation, engineers will start their testing there. They will then check our network equipment throughout the area to try and identify any problems, before trying to restore power.

Our estimated time frame of 23:30 and 00:30 hasn't changed, but if this is not successful it's possible that a cable repair may be needed. This can involve ground excavations, traffic management equipment or specialist teams. As soon as our staff can safely update us, we'll give you the latest news. Sent by Bradley  at 20:26.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Thanks for your patience today. We know a power cut can be difficult, especially in colder weather.

Many properties have gas hobs, which can still be used in a power cut for cooking, or heating water for drinks and sterilisation of baby bottles. The spark to ignite the hob will not work however, so if you do use it please take extra care when using other ignition sources like matches or lighters. Even in daytime, the light in your house may be low in a power cut, so only do this if you are confident it can be done safely.

If you have any questions or concerns, our team are always on hand to help.

We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
As a result of this. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 15:30 and 16:30. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Kevin

Sent by Jack at 23:18 - We can now confirm that all power in the area should be back on. Our engineers had to unexpectedly turn off the power to 1075 customers in the Brandon IP27 area to safely investigate and repair a network fault.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. Please rest assured our staff will continue to work around the clock to keep the lights on.

If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Jack at 21:51 - We're very sorry we've had to switch off your electricity. Our engineers have turned off the power in the Brandon IP27 area for safety so they can repair some network damage. Our estimated time to have your power back on is between 02:00 and 03:00, however, this may need to change later depending on how our works progress. If you'd like more information about why we sometimes have to switch power off to work; here's a short video https://UKPN.short.gy/Isol. We'll keep you updated with progress.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Hi. This is Bev from the messaging team here at UK Power Networks. I know that the bad weather brought by Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things difficult, and having a power cut on top of that is an extra worry.

I just wanted to reach out and say that as our field engineers and control room work to get your lights back on just as soon as they can, my team and I are going to be here keeping you updated with the latest.

We're only human, and as you can imagine, we have a lot of power cuts to fix so while we'll send you the clearest information we can, updates may come less often than usual and we might make the odd typo. For now, we hope you're managing okay, and we'll be in touch again soon.

Steps.Message:
We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
We think it's unlikely we will be able to restore your electricity tonight. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 19:00 and 20:00. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Will at 02:39.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Will at 00:15 - Thanks for your patience; I'll be on hand to update you as our staff work on repairs, and I just wanted to give you the latest from site. We can now confirm that a tree has fallen on to our overhead cables. Although we know what's causing your power cut, we still need to remove the tree and repair any damage to the cables. To do this we will send a specialist teams and equipment. Its likely this won't now be until the morning but once they are on their way we'll be able to advise a new estimated time frame for the repair. For more information about this type of fault; here's a short video https://UKPN.short.gy/OH.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Milly at 22:24 - Hello. Thanks for your patience tonight, I can see from our engineer's notes that your lights may have come on and gone back off several times since we've been made aware of the issue, and I'm sorry if this is causing you any worry. We are experiencing an overhead network fault and our staff work to divert power when a fault like this happens. Sometimes, these diversions can be unsuccessful, so we have to try routing power another way; this is why your lights are going off and on. We are currently estimating to restore power between 02:00-03:00 If at any point your power comes back on, you can always stop SMS updates here - https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 01:07 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

To stop receiving texts, just follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Sent by Talie at 01:14.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Theo at 00:05 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an overhead network fault affecting 178 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 04:30 and 05:30. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Will at 01:25 - We can now confirm that all power in the Selwyn Road area should be back on. The issue was caused by an unexpected fault with some of our network equipment, which our engineers have now replaced.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. Please rest assured our staff will continue to work around the clock to keep the lights on.

If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Engineers have arrived on site to investigate what we believe to be an issue at the local substation in the Selwyn Road area. Using an average timescale for this type of issue, we're looking to have you back on between 04:30 and 05:30, however we must stress that this time may change, depending on what our staff find.

We know that a power cut can be very disruptive; we understand this can greatly impact your daily activities and we want to support you however we can. We'll update you with all of our progress, but for more information about this type of fault; here's a short YouTube video https://UKPN.short.gy/fuse. Sent by Will at 01:20.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.
